books.section: Topic 4.12 African Americans in the Early Republic, B. The Cultures of African-American Communities

stimulus.text:
Free Black men organized to defend their rights. In September 1830, delegates from several Northern states met at Mother Bethel Church in Philadelphia, chose Richard Allen as president, and formed a society to improve the condition of free people of color and plan a settlement in Canada.

At the same time, Northern states were narrowing Black men’s rights: New York’s 1821 constitution dropped the property test for white voters but kept a $250 property requirement for Black voters, and Pennsylvania’s 1838 constitution limited the vote to white men. New York had ended slavery only gradually, with final emancipation in 1827.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the first National Negro Convention, September 1830, from John W. Cromwell, The Early Negro Convention Movement, and of the voting restrictions in the New York constitution of 1821 and the Pennsylvania constitution of 1838.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Cromwell, The Early Negro Convention Movement
stem: The 1830 convention best shows that free Black leaders

options.text: accepted colonization to Liberia as their best hope
options.misconception: They planned a settlement in Canada and opposed colonization.

options.text: refused to meet together until slavery ended
options.misconception: They met in 1830 while slavery stood.

options.text: organized nationally to defend their interests and plan their future
asked white abolitionists to choose their leaders for them

rationales.A: The convention planned a settlement in Canada, not in Liberia. Its leaders opposed colonization.
rationales.B: The delegates met in 1830, with slavery still standing. They did not wait for it to end first.
rationales.C: Delegates from several Northern states met, chose Allen as president, and formed a society to improve their condition.
rationales.D: The delegates chose their own president, Richard Allen. No white abolitionist chose for them.
rationales.general:
1. Note the meeting. Delegates from several Northern states gathered at Mother Bethel in Philadelphia.
2. Note what they did. They chose Allen president and formed a society to improve their condition and plan a Canadian settlement.
3. Name the move. National organizing by Black leaders themselves.
Background: Richard Allen founded the AME Church and hosted the convention at Mother Bethel.
Remember: a convention is a people deciding together; ask what they decided.
